problem_class.label: nonconvex
problem_class.details: Unconstrained differentiable f on a second-countable real Hilbert space E; ∇f is globally L-Lipschitz and f(x0)−f(x)≤Δ for every x. Convexity and attainment of the infimum are not required. L>0 and Δ≥0.

oracle.label: stochastic_gradient
oracle.details: A query x returns g(x,ω). Calls 2j and 2j+1 share the same hidden sample ωj; samples across pairs are IID. Only oracle replies are exposed, with each evaluation counted separately. Neither integrability nor unbiasedness of g is assumed. All Params, including L, κ, r, Δ, ε and x0, are public; f, g and the sampling laws are hidden.
oracle.evidence: LongTails/Setups/RelativeEnergySymmetricNonconvex.lean: spec.Public, spec.publicInput, spec.admissible and oracle law P.map (fun ξ k => ξ (k / 2)); LongTails/Template.lean: Algorithm, Oracle, executeWithTrace, Convergence; LongTails/Setups/StochasticGeneralizedSmoothAndConvex.lean: IID.

distinctive_assumptions.label: gradient_similarity
distinctive_assumptions.details: For every x,y, E[(‖e(x,ω)−e(y,ω)‖/(r+‖e(x,ω)‖+‖e(y,ω)‖))²]≤κ²‖x−y‖², where κ≥0 and both errors use the same sample. This controls normalized error increments, not unnormalized mean-square gradient differences or pointwise relative gradient error.

distinctive_assumptions.label: heavy_tailed_noise
distinctive_assumptions.details: Writing e(x,ω)=g(x,ω)−∇f(x), the law of e(x,ω) equals that of −e(x,ω), and Pr(‖e(x,ω)‖>r)≤1/64 uniformly in x, with r≥0. No finite noise moment or density is required.
distinctive_assumptions.evidence: LongTails/Setups/RelativeEnergySymmetricNonconvex.lean: spec.valid; symmetry and tail-probability clauses of spec.admissible.

distinctive_assumptions.label: other
distinctive_assumptions.details: The ambient space may be infinite-dimensional: E is a complete real inner-product space with its Borel measurable structure and second-countable topology. Oracle dependence consists of prescribed consecutive sample pairs, independent across pairs.

accuracy.label: gradient_norm
accuracy.details: Return a measurable E-valued output X with integrable ‖∇f(X)‖ and E‖∇f(X)‖≤ε, ε>0. The criterion uses the first power of the norm and applies to the returned point.

accuracy.label: expected
accuracy.details: Expectation is over the joint algorithm and oracle randomness. The extracted result supplies a fixed oracle-call cap, rather than an expected stopping cost.

setup_category.label: non_standard
setup_category.reason: The standard smooth nonconvex objective is combined with moment-free symmetric noise, a quantile bound, normalized mean-square error increments, and prescribed paired sample reuse. These are unusual oracle assumptions.

descriptionHtml:
Nonconvex Optimization with Symmetric Noise

We consider minimizing a differentiable, possibly nonconvex function f:E→R on a separable real Hilbert space E. Its gradient is L-Lipschitz, with L>0, and a given point x0∈E satisfies f(x0)−infx∈Ef(x)≤Δ, where Δ≥0. The oracle returns g(x,ξ)∈E, with symmetric noise having tail radius r≥0 and relative-energy regularity parameter κ≥0. Consecutive pairs of calls share a sample ξ, independently across pairs. For ε>0, the goal is a measurable output x¯∈E satisfying E∥∇f(x¯)∥≤ε, where expectation includes sampling and independent algorithm randomness.

The optimization problem is infx∈Ef(x). The norm ∥⋅∥ is induced by the inner product on E, equipped with its Borel sigma-algebra. Let Ω be a measurable sample space. The algorithm receives E, Ω, L, κ, r, Δ, ε, and x0; it accesses f through the oracle described below.

Our assumptions:

Assumption 1 (Smoothness and initial gap). The function f is Fréchet differentiable everywhere, and, for every x,y∈E, ∥∇f(x)−∇f(y)∥≤L∥x−y∥,f(x0)−f(x)≤Δ.

Assumption 2 (Symmetry and tail radius). There exist a probability measure ν on Ω and a jointly measurable map g:E×Ω→E. Define the noise by e(x,ω)=g(x,ω)−∇f(x). For every x∈E, under ξ∼ν, e(x,ξ)=d−e(x,ξ),Pξ∼ν(∥e(x,ξ)∥>r)≤164. Here equality in distribution is equality of the induced probability measures on E.

Assumption 3 (Relative-energy regularity). For every x,y∈E, the noise evaluated with the same sample satisfies Eξ∼ν[(∥e(x,ξ)−e(y,ξ)∥r+∥e(x,ξ)∥+∥e(y,ξ)∥)2]≤κ2∥x−y∥2. The ratio is defined to be zero when its denominator is zero.

Oracle queries may be made at any point of E. Let (ξj)j≥0 be measurable, mutually independent sample variables, each with law ν, and independent of the algorithm’s randomness. Index calls starting at zero. At query xk∈E, call k returns g(xk,ξ⌊k/2⌋). Thus calls 2j and 2j+1 use the same sample, including when the second query depends on the first reply.

After the allotted oracle calls, the output x¯ must be measurable and satisfy EP∥∇f(x¯)∥≤ε,∥∇f(x¯)∥∈L1(P), where P is the joint law of the samples and the algorithm’s independent randomness.

comparisonHtml:
On a separable real Hilbert space with its Borel structure, f is differentiable, ∇f is L-Lipschitz, and f(x0)−inff≤Δ. The jointly measurable oracle g(x,ξ) has marginally symmetric noise ζx=g(x,ξ)−∇f(x) with Pr(∥ζx∥>r)≤1/64 and E[(∥ζx−ζy∥/(r+∥ζx∥+∥ζy∥))2]≤κ2∥x−y∥2. Samples are IID across query pairs, with a shared sample within each pair; no noise moments are assumed. Here L,ε>0 and r,κ,Δ≥0. The target is a measurable output x^ with integrable gradient norm and ∫∥∇f(x^(ω))∥dP(ω)≤ε, for the execution law P.

import LongTails.Template
import LongTails.Setups.StochasticGeneralizedSmoothAndConvex
import Mathlib.Analysis.Calculus.Gradient.Basic

open MeasureTheory

namespace LongTails.Setups.RelativeEnergySymmetricNonconvex

open OracleTemplate

structure Params where
  E : Type
  [normedE : NormedAddCommGroup E]
  [innerE : InnerProductSpace ℝ E]
  [completeE : CompleteSpace E]
  [measurableE : MeasurableSpace E]
  [borelE : BorelSpace E]
  [countableE : SecondCountableTopology E]
  Ω : Type
  [measurableΩ : MeasurableSpace Ω]
  L : ℝ
  κ : ℝ
  r : ℝ
  Δ : ℝ
  ε : ℝ
  x0 : E

attribute [instance] Params.normedE Params.innerE Params.completeE Params.measurableE
  Params.borelE Params.countableE Params.measurableΩ

abbrev spec : Setup where
  Params := Params
  Public := Params
  Instance q := q.E → ℝ
  Query q := q.E
  Reply q := q.E
  Output q := q.E
  publicInput q := q
  valid q := 0 < q.L ∧ 0 ≤ q.κ ∧ 0 ≤ q.r ∧ 0 ≤ q.Δ ∧ 0 < q.ε
  admissible q f O :=
    ∃ (g : q.E → q.Ω → q.E) (p : ProbabilityMeasure q.Ω) (P : ProbabilityMeasure (ℕ → q.Ω)),
      LongTails.Setups.StochasticGeneralizedSmoothAndConvex.IID
        (fun k (ξ : ℕ → q.Ω) => ξ k) (p : Measure _) (P : Measure _) ∧
      O = { Seed := fun _ => q.Ω
            law := P.map (fun ξ k => ξ (k / 2))
            answer := fun _ (_, x) ω => g x ω } ∧
      (∀ x, HasGradientAt f (gradient f x) x) ∧
      (∀ x y, ‖gradient f x - gradient f y‖ ≤ q.L * ‖x - y‖) ∧
      (∀ x, f q.x0 - f x ≤ q.Δ) ∧
      Measurable (Function.uncurry g) ∧
      (∀ x, (p : Measure _).map (fun ω => g x ω - gradient f x) =
        (p : Measure _).map (fun ω => -(g x ω - gradient f x))) ∧
      (∀ x, (p : Measure _).real {ω | q.r < ‖g x ω - gradient f x‖} ≤ 1 / 64) ∧
      (∀ x y, ∫ ω, (‖(g x ω - gradient f x) - (g y ω - gradient f y)‖ /
        (q.r + ‖g x ω - gradient f x‖ + ‖g y ω - gradient f y‖)) ^ 2 ∂p ≤
        q.κ ^ 2 * ‖x - y‖ ^ 2)
  successful q f output P :=
    Measurable output ∧
      Integrable (fun ω => ‖gradient f (output ω)‖) (P : Measure _) ∧
      ∫ ω, ‖gradient f (output ω)‖ ∂(P : Measure _) ≤ q.ε

end LongTails.Setups.RelativeEnergySymmetricNonconvex
